correctness.rationale: Every independent dominating configuration on a path is represented by gaps of one/two zeros and zero/one endpoint padding. Counting gives n=3m-2-a+e, yielding sharp achievable maximum a=3m-n for ceil(n/3)<=m<=floor((n-1)/2), and a=ceil(n/2)-1 for m=ceil(n/2). The game payoff gives W=nb(e*)+ce*(ta-m). Exact affine score differences yield the complete n-parity-specific classification, including n=2,4, degeneracies and ties. Independent exhaustive rational verification for orders 2..23 checks profiles and optimal sets, and the analytical proof handles all n. Restrictions to specialized NE prevent unsupported global welfare implications.

originality.rationale: The game and MIS-specialist identification are established in [1] and are treated as premises, not innovations. Inspected relevant primary work supplies neither the all-n welfare-maximizer classification among specialized equilibria nor its interior double threshold and minimum 12-player three-regime case. Actual Research-record searches for the claim and graph reformulations yielded related but not implying records. The possibility of uninspected equivalent combinatorial optimization or followup results remains an explicit risk; this is a best-knowledge, non-independent assessment.
residual_risks: The Corbo–Calvó-Armengol–Parkes local contribution game has only an abstract-level comparison here; its different payoff model is unlikely to imply arbitrary-benefit thresholds, but its full work was not inspected.
An equivalent reformulation in less discoverable domination, independent-set optimization, or subsequent public-goods papers may exist.
Best-knowledge self-review originality assessment is not independent certification.

value.rationale: This is a complete all-parameter structural classification for public-goods provision on natural line networks in the baseline foundational game, not an arbitrary parameter slice. Its two universal thresholds change the welfare-optimal specialization density, and n=12 is a sharp smallest network with three strict regimes. The exact finite-length policy comparisons are not established by the broader existence and welfare bounds in inspected sources. Explicit limitation: only specialized equilibria are ranked.
